To solve this problem, we can use the following formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is $400,$ and the percentage is $0.25%.$ 

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
0.25%=0.25÷100=0.0025
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =0.25%\times 400 \\  & =0.0025\times 400 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $0.25%$ of $400$ is $1.$

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
0.25%=\frac{0.25}{100}=\frac{0.25\times 100}{100\times 100}=\frac{25}{10,000}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =0.25%\times 400 \\  & =\frac{25}{10,000}\times 400 \\  & =\frac{10,000}{10,000} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $0.25%$ of $400$ is $1.$
